newsitem.title: FRANCE: Analysts see Zeneca or Warner-Lambert in Sanofi deal.
newsitem.headline: Analysts see Zeneca or Warner-Lambert in Sanofi deal.

text.p: Financial analysts said on Thursday that Britain's Zeneca and Warner-Lambert Co of the U.S. were best placed for a possible alliance with French drugs and beauty products group Sanofi.
They said that while these companies' market values are much higher than Sanofi's, in sales terms the companies are comparable.
Oil group Elf Aquitaine, a 53 percent holder of Sanofi stock, on Thursday said that it wnated Sanofi to merge with another drugs group and added it did not need to keep a majority stake.
"It would be desirable for Sanofi to move nearer other pharmaceutical laboratories, through a merger, in order to speed up its development and increase its profitability," Elf said.

The announcement immediately fuelled old rumours that Sanofi was at the point of merging with Rhone-Poulenc's Franco-American drugs unit Rhone-Poulenc Rorer. But Rhone-Poulenc managing director Igor Landau, at a news conference to announce an animal health joint venture deal with Merck and Co Inc, said the group had no interest at all in another drugs alliance and would concentrate on internal growth.

"We are the seventh biggest drugs group in the world, we are the leader in the six therapeutic areas in which we are active, we have our hands full with the launch of new products and we are not interested at all in any alliance," Landau said.
But industry observers said everything was possible in the highly volatile pharmaceutical market where companies are joining to spread the costs and risks of developing new drugs.

And Rhone-Poulenc Rorer, with its acqusition of Fisons of Britain last year, has been playing its full role in the industry restructuring, be it at a smaller scale than the Novartis merger of Ciba-Geigy AG and Sandoz AG or the link between Hoechst, Marion Merrell Dow and Roussel-Uclaf

Some analysts said that there could be an alliance between Sanofi and Bristol-Myers Squibb with which Sanofi already cooperates for some compounds which have yielded two of its new drugs Clopidogrel and Irebesartan.
But market specialists said Bristol Myers' market value was some $53 billion, against $9.5 for Sanofi.
"The distribution of power is far too unequal. Elf wants to reduce its stake in Sanofi but certainly not sell its subsidiary to Bristol Myers Squibb," said an analyst.
Another rumoured possibility of a link with Synthelabo, controlled by L'Oreal, was seen as unlikley because it would not allow Sanofi to re-inforce its position in the U.S.
However, one analysts said that Sanofi, led by Jean Francois Dehecq, could be interested in the strong positions in the Japanse market held by Synthelabo.
Sanofi closed 6.24 percent higher at 494 francs.
